gist: Despite the generic title, Jordi Visser argues AI and crypto are one inevitable trade (tokenization, agentic commerce) and that Bitcoin bottomed this week, citing TradFi signals: a rare quality-to-beta reversal, an ending hedge-fund de-grossing, and broad disinflation that makes a Fed 50bp move unnecessary. He frames the AI correction as capital-supply driven, not a bubble, and discloses buying Zcash.

themes.theme: AI and crypto as one inevitable trade

insights.claim: Jordi Visser argues AI and crypto are the same trade: tokenization and agentic commerce cannot accelerate without both AI and crypto, so allocation decisions between them should be treated as one exposure.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Size AI and crypto as correlated, mutually dependent exposures rather than diversifiers.
insights.quote: they are exactly the same trade. They are completely aligned.

insights.claim: Visser rejects following the Fed liquidity cycle: money printing lifted assets to current levels, but moving a roughly $3 trillion crypto market cap further requires fundamentals because liquidity comes from innovation.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch tokenization/agentic-commerce adoption, not central-bank balance sheets, as the driver of the next crypto leg.
insights.quote: Liquidity comes from innovation.

insights.claim: Using the iPhone era as a template, Visser says from 2007 to the ChatGPT launch macro-watching made no money; MSCI World ex US was unchanged over that span while US software and the Mag 7 captured the value.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: During exponential innovation waves, stay concentrated in the innovation leaders and ignore month-to-month macro noise.
insights.quote: MSCI World ex US was unchanged from the day the iPhone came out in 2007 till the day when ChatGPT came out.

insights.claim: Visser believes AI will impair the growth of most public companies and make them more volatile and less investable, shifting capital formation to on-chain tokens (a 'mag billion' instead of the Mag 7), which is why he calls Bitcoin the purest AI trade.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Expect equity-market disruption (e.g. SaaS) to push capital toward on-chain assets; Bitcoin as the proxy.
insights.quote: I believe AI will destroy all public companies or at least the majority of them

insights.claim: Tokenization is inevitable partly because AI will enable fakes of everything, making clear blockchain-based ownership records a security necessity, alongside users holding all their ownership on their phones.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Deepfake/AI fraud risk is a structural demand driver for on-chain ownership and tokenization infrastructure.
insights.quote: AI will enable people to create fakes of everything

insights.claim: Visser argues US political noise (Democrats, Jensen Huang headlines) will not stop AI because it is global: other countries, especially in Asia, would welcome data-center builds if the US slows, in exchange for access to compute.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Don't sell AI exposure on US political headlines; the buildout relocates rather than stops.

themes.theme: TradFi signals calling a crypto bottom

insights.claim: Visser believes Bitcoin and the broader digital-asset market bottomed this week, based on signals that the AI equity trade is bottoming.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Treat AI-equity strength as a leading indicator for re-entering crypto.
insights.quote: I believe Bitcoin and the crypto digital asset world bottom this week

insights.claim: A two-day 16% move of beta over quality has only occurred in March 2009 (S&P low at 666), March 2020, June 2020 and November 2022, each near major market and Bitcoin lows; it just happened again.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A sharp quality-to-beta rotation is Visser's historical buy signal for risk assets including crypto.
insights.quote: That is a 16% move.

insights.claim: Visser attributes crypto's decline since the September peak roughly 50/50 to liquidity headwinds (rising rates and oil) and the AI-trade/hedge-fund unwind, where long-standing funds went from up 45% to down 10% in four months in an unwind comparable to COVID and the GFC.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Crypto weakness was forced de-grossing, not a broken thesis; it should recover as the unwind ends.
insights.quote: Bitcoin is never going to do well during a large de grossing.

insights.claim: Bitcoin divided by gold synthetically tracks Ethereum, and Bitcoin outperforming gold signals genuine inflows into digital assets rather than war- or debasement-driven buying; its two-day bounce is a leading bottom signal.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Use BTC/gold as a gauge for Ethereum and for healthy crypto demand.
insights.quote: Bitcoin over gold synthetically is Ethereum.

insights.claim: Bitcoin has tracked the SMH semiconductor ETF since September, while the Euro bank index and the US leveraged loan index have already bottomed and rallied, implying Bitcoin is lagging broad impulsive risk-on signals.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Lagging Bitcoin versus already-turned risk proxies suggests catch-up potential.

insights.claim: Visser says liquidity is driven by the dollar rather than central-bank cycles, and that asset-level changes lead; the late-October turn came from selling exhaustion, not any change in the liquidity cycle.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch the dollar and cross-asset price action rather than central-bank liquidity metrics.
insights.quote: These liquidity cycles that people talk about relative to the Fed, the central banks are ridiculous. It's related to the dollar.

insights.claim: The inverted quality factor correlates with Bitcoin; a big Friday quality-versus-beta move led Visser to reject the AI 'dead cat bounce' call, and Monday rallied strongly.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Quality-vs-beta factor moves can front-run both AI equities and crypto.
insights.quote: I disagreed with everyone that said AI was a dead cat bounce

themes.theme: AI equity correction was capital supply, not bubble

insights.claim: Visser attributes the AI correction to massive equity supply, starting with Google selling $80 billion of equity in May and continuing with SpaceX and other raises, into a fully positioned hedge-fund world with trillions in leveraged ETFs, not to a bubble bursting.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: AI drawdowns driven by issuance are buyable once supply is absorbed; crypto lacks this capital-supply overhang.
insights.quote: This had nothing to do with a bubble unwind. This just had to do with the massive capital that was coming.

insights.claim: Anthropic's valuation fell from over $2 trillion (perhaps $3 trillion) to an expected IPO around $1.5 trillion, which Visser blames on the AI trade selling off.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Private AI valuations reprice with public AI sentiment; IPO pricing is a sentiment gauge.

insights.claim: Visser sees the Democratic sweep as bullish because it removes bubble risk and accelerates Asia, where Taiwan, Korea and China intervened this week to support stock markets since AI capital needs must be raised when stock prices are high.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Asian policy support for equities is a tailwind for AI capital raising and Asian AI beneficiaries.
insights.quote: I think the democratic sweep is bullish.

insights.claim: Visser says Waller and Logan's talk of a 50bp move is unnecessary: the market assigns only about a 10% chance, prices one move in December and none in January, so a 25bp outcome should be read as positive news; he cites 22V's Gerard McDonald as agreeing.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Fade the 50bp scare; a 25bp outcome removes a tail risk for crypto and AI.
insights.quote: I don't know why they would go 50.

insights.claim: Core CPI six- and nine-month averages are at or below levels seen when the Fed was previously set to cut, core PCE is 3.12, and alternative measures (Atlanta Fed sticky, Dallas Fed trimmed mean, Cleveland median) are near the year's lows.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Underlying inflation does not justify aggressive Fed tightening.

insights.claim: Visser shows a disinflation pipeline: Brent crude is flat on a 175-day rate of change, so oil will be flat year-over-year by March; food and livestock futures peaked in September; DRAM prices fell from 9x to 3x year-over-year; two-year inflation expectations are below the year's start; and Goldman Sachs sees a 110bp drop in PCE next year.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Second-derivative inflation is collapsing, which supports lower yields and risk assets.
insights.quote: These are all second derivative, but that's what you care about for year-over-year.

insights.claim: The 10-year yield jumped from about 4.70% to 5.40% while oil rose toward 120, hurting crypto; yields are now around 5%, 40bp off the high, and bond volatility peaked in October and has fallen sharply.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Easing rates and bond vol remove a key crypto headwind.
insights.quote: we are still 40 basis points off the high

insights.claim: JGB yields have fallen back to May levels and are testing their 200-day moving average, which they have not closed below since 2024; Visser treats a break as a signal the worst of the global liquidity headwinds is over.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch a JGB yield close below the 200-day as confirmation for crypto and AI tailwinds.
insights.quote: We have not closed below the 200-day moving average in JGB since 2024.

insights.claim: Bitcoin's rally coincided with agentic-commerce catalysts (Instinct AI, Grok bot, Meta's Muse, Robinhood chain), while the drawdown came with rising rates and oil, Chamath's Bitcoin-to-zero hot take and the Binance hack.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Agentic-commerce launches are fundamental crypto catalysts; macro noise temporarily overrode them.

insights.claim: On four-hour Bitcoin charts Visser looks for wick-heavy buying and bullish RSI divergence; he sees this around the 75 area with a slightly lower low, and likes the setup especially because it held up on bad news, with Bitcoin down 4% month to date.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Short-term RSI divergence near the 75 level is his tactical entry trigger.
insights.quote: I'm looking for a divergence where the RSI's don't make new lows, but prices do.

insights.claim: Visser treats Bitcoin as the S&P and the broader crypto index as the Nasdaq/QQQ: a higher-beta basket that should outperform when Bitcoin rises and underperform when it falls.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Use altcoin baskets for beta on a Bitcoin upturn, not as a hedge.
insights.quote: Bitcoin is the most important thing. I view it as the S&P

insights.claim: Visser says he bought some crypto on the recent weakness, mainly Zcash, because it had traded off to a level he liked.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Disclosed positioning: Zcash added on the dip.
insights.quote: mainly in Zcash
